correctness.rationale: For arbitrary pointed genuine metric M over real scalars, the molecular unit ball of F(M) reduces ||D_lambda|| to sup images of (δx−δy)/d(x,y). For any triple o,x,y the admissible 1-Lipschitz values (u,v) form the exact polygon |u|≤a, |v|≤b, |u−v|≤c by McShane extension; its six vertices are ±(a,b), ±(a,a−c), ±(b−c,b). Maximizing λ_x u−λ_y v gives H_xy exactly. Spokes yield |λ_x|. A finite molecular supremum is necessary/sufficient for continuous bounded extension on completed F(M), including infinite nondiscrete M and degenerate triangle inequalities. For coordinate cuts λ∈{0,1}, mixed pairs give a/c; all-active give 1; for signs λ∈{−1,1}, opposite pairs yield (a+b)/c. This gives exact finite basis constants and rooted-star contractivity. Verified the independent mathematical polygon and selector inequalities, inspected deterministic exact-rational local verifier, but general validity comes from duality/extension rather than its 7000 cases.
residual_risks: Infinite Dirac family need not be a Schauder basis; norm formula is for the algebraic diagonal and bounded extensions, not an unconditional infinite coordinate expansion.
